- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes; apply a 1-2 day lag correction or dampen upward momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5-10%.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3-5% gap), model may be overconfident; adjust downward by 2-5% for next period.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underperforms; add 1-3% buffer to forecast to account for suppressed volatility.
